inferred_requirements.title: Real-Time ARINC 429 Telemetry Frame Ingestion to Buffer
inferred_requirements.description: The Flight Data Recorder (FDR) telemetry software shall continuously ingest 32-bit ARINC 429 bus word frames from the receiver interface into an in-memory buffer in real time.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated in prompt: 'Implement real-time flight data recorder buffer synchronization that flushes ARINC 429 bus frames'.

inferred_requirements.title: Emergency Telemetry Flush to Solid-State Crash-Survivable Memory on Power Loss
inferred_requirements.description: Upon detection of an imminent primary power failure, the system shall flush pending uncommitted ARINC 429 telemetry frames from volatile memory into solid-state Crash-Survivable Memory Units (CSMU).
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated in prompt: 'flushes ARINC 429 bus frames to solid-state crash-survivable memory on power loss'.

inferred_requirements.title: DO-178C Static Memory Pre-Allocation
inferred_requirements.description: All telemetry buffers, ring queues, and Direct Memory Access (DMA) transfer descriptors shall be statically allocated at compile time; runtime dynamic heap allocation (e.g., malloc/free) is strictly prohibited.
inferred_requirements.justification: Step 1: DO-178C Level A/B safety-critical avionics standards strictly disallow unbounded heap allocation to eliminate risks of memory fragmentation and non-deterministic execution times. -> Step 2: Unpredictable allocation latency or memory exhaustion during high-rate telemetry capture could cause catastrophic frame loss or system lockups. -> Step 3: Therefore, static pre-allocation of fixed-size data structures with bounded execution time is technically necessary to guarantee deterministic memory safety.

inferred_requirements.title: Ingestion into Deterministic Ring Buffer
inferred_requirements.description: Ingested ARINC 429 frames shall be queued into a deterministic, lock-free circular ring buffer using atomic head/tail index tracking to decouple high-frequency RX interrupt routines from slower non-volatile write routines.
inferred_requirements.justification: Step 1: ARINC 429 bus frames arrive asynchronously across high-speed bus lines and must be captured within strict ISR deadlines. -> Step 2: Blocking synchronization primitives (e.g., mutexes, semaphores) cause priority inversion and unbounded ISR jitter. -> Step 3: Therefore, a lock-free deterministic ring buffer is technically necessary to safely queue frames across execution contexts without race conditions or dropped frames.

inferred_requirements.title: Emergency Flush on Power Loss Interrupt
inferred_requirements.description: The system shall attach a dedicated top-priority Power-Fail Interrupt (PFI/NMI) handler to hardware voltage monitor lines to immediately preempt standard tasks and initiate the crash-survivable memory flush sequence.
inferred_requirements.justification: Step 1: Aircraft electrical power loss events during catastrophic incidents occur instantaneously, leaving minimal residual power. -> Step 2: Polling-based power monitoring introduces scheduling latency that risks total power collapse before write routines can start. -> Step 3: Therefore, a hardware-vectored Non-Maskable / Power-Fail Interrupt (NMI/PFI) handler is technically necessary to immediately trigger the emergency flush without software polling delays.

inferred_requirements.title: Hold-Up Capacitor Energy Budget Time Window Enforcement (<=50ms Flush Deadline)
inferred_requirements.description: The entire emergency volatile-to-nonvolatile buffer flush sequence shall complete within a worst-case execution time (WCET) of <= 50ms from power-fail interrupt assertion, matching the hardware hold-up capacitor power reserve budget.
inferred_requirements.justification: Step 1: Airborne solid-state recorders rely on auxiliary hold-up capacitors that provide a finite energy window (typically <= 50ms to 200ms) upon loss of main 28V DC / 115V AC aircraft power. -> Step 2: If the non-volatile write cycle exceeds this capacitor discharge window, the write will abort mid-page, resulting in uncommitted buffer loss and flash sector corruption. -> Step 3: Therefore, enforcing a strict <= 50ms flush deadline with verified WCET is technically necessary to guarantee full data persistence before capacitor energy depletion.

inferred_requirements.title: ARINC 429 Parity and CRC Verification
inferred_requirements.description: The receiver pipeline shall validate the parity bit (bit 32, odd/even per bus config) of each ARINC 429 word and compute block-level CRC integrity checks before committing frames to the telemetry buffer; corrupted words shall be flagged with error status.
inferred_requirements.justification: Step 1: ARINC 429 specification mandates odd (or optionally even) parity on bit 32 to detect transmission errors caused by avionics EMI/RFI noise. -> Step 2: Committing corrupted or unverified telemetry frames to crash-survivable storage impairs post-incident crash investigation and violates data authenticity standards. -> Step 3: Therefore, validating parity and CRC prior to buffer persistence is technically necessary to ensure data integrity in the recorded flight record.

inferred_requirements.title: Non-Volatile Flash Wear-Leveling and Circular Overwrite
inferred_requirements.description: The solid-state crash-survivable memory management layer shall implement deterministic flash wear-leveling and circular block overwrite algorithms to evenly distribute write/erase cycles while maintaining the mandatory rolling flight duration telemetry history.
inferred_requirements.justification: Step 1: Solid-state NAND/NOR flash cells have finite physical program/erase (P/E) endurance limits. -> Step 2: Continuous flight recording writes millions of frames over operational lifetimes, which would exhaust localized flash blocks rapidly without wear-leveling. -> Step 3: Therefore, deterministic wear-leveling coupled with circular block overwrite is technically necessary to prevent physical media failure while maintaining compliant continuous rolling flight recording.

inferred_requirements.title: Crash-Survivable Memory Physical Protection Compliance
inferred_requirements.description: The memory storage interface shall write to solid-state memory modules rated for EUROCAE ED-112A / FAA TSO-C124b crash survivability (impact shock, penetration resistance, static crush, and high-temperature fire resistance).
inferred_requirements.justification: Supported by the prompt specification of 'crash-survivable memory' and standard aerospace black box certification standards (ED-112A / TSO-C124b).

inferred_requirements.title: ARINC 429 Channel Transmission Bit Rate
inferred_requirements.description: Operational bit rate of the ARINC 429 input channels (Low Speed: 12.5 kbps vs High Speed: 100 kbps) and total physical receiver channel count.
inferred_requirements.justification: The ARINC 429 standard defines two transmission speeds: 12.5 kbps and 100 kbps. The prompt leaves the target baud rate and channel multiplexing topology unstated.
